passage: My name is Amandeep. When Anjali asked me to take a third role in the college clubs, this time as treasurer, my first reaction was yes. I always say yes. But I opened my timetable that night and counted. Classes, two lab days, the debate club on Tuesdays, the film club on Fridays, and a job on Saturdays. There was no free evening left. I realised that a full schedule with one more item does not make one more item, it makes everything worse. Sleep would go first. So the next morning I told Anjali honestly that I could not do it well and did not want to do it badly. She thanked me for saying so early.

Faculty adviser's note – Seema, student clubs
Tarun came to see me today about the offer to be treasurer of the photography club. He is already secretary of the debate society and runs the coding club's workshops. I expected him to say yes; he usually does.
Instead he showed me his week on paper: classes, two club roles, a tutoring job at weekends, and about five hours of sleep a night for the last month. 'If I add a third role, something breaks, and it'll probably be my health or my grades,' he said. 'I don't want to do all three badly.'
He asked me how to say no without letting the club down. I suggested being honest and naming someone else. He wrote to the club that evening, thanked them, explained, and recommended a second-year he thought would be good.
I was glad. It is not easy at nineteen to turn down something you would enjoy.

qa.q: How much sleep had Tarun been getting over the last month?
qa.a: About five hours of sleep a night.

qa.q: What was Tarun feeling when he said he didn't want to do all three badly?
qa.a: He was worried that overload would hurt his health or grades, and chose to protect his sleep over a role he might enjoy.

qa.q: What else could Tarun do to keep his two roles manageable?
qa.a: Look at the hours each role takes and protect a regular bedtime, reviewing the week again if sleep slips.

qa.q: How might the photography club feel about his reply?
qa.a: They may be disappointed but respect the honesty, and they have a recommended second-year to ask.

grounding: Shows a student with a full schedule declining a third club role honestly and suggesting someone else, to protect sleep and avoid overload.

Friday night
Parul asked me today to co-run the college film festival. Three weeks of work, starting Monday. My heart jumped. I love films.
And then I opened my planner. Two quizzes next week. The research internship form due on the 20th. My café shifts on Saturday and Sunday. NSS on Wednesday. I'm already sleeping at one most nights.
I sat on the library steps for a long time. If I say yes, something gives, and I know what gives: sleep first, then the quizzes, then the form. I've done this before and it hurt everything.
So I texted Parul: 'I'd love to, honestly, but my weeks are full till the 20th and I'd do a bad job. Could I help with just the poster design after that?' She replied with a sad face and then, 'Deal.'
It stings a bit. But I'm going to bed at eleven tonight.
– Parveen

qa.a: Parul is briefly disappointed, sending a sad face, but values the honesty and accepts the smaller offer.

grounding: Shows a student who sees a full week, declines a new commitment honestly and offers a smaller role later, to protect sleep and studies.
